 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. LeBron James is set to return to the Philadelphia 76ers lineup for Sunday's home game against the Indiana Pacers. The 41-year-old star missed Thursday's victory over the Toronto Raptors to manage low back and sciatica issues, marking his third absence in the team's first 13 games. This is a massive boost for a team that has struggled to find consistency without its veteran leader.
 The Sixers have been careful with James' workload all season. He has not played on consecutive days yet this year as the team manages his health. Nick Nurse now faces a tough choice on how much to play him before the team travels to Brooklyn for a road game on Monday. James struggled in his last outing against Boston, scoring only 11 points on 4-of-12 shooting in 29 minutes. In his first season with the Sixers, he maintains averages of 15.1 points, 7.2 rebounds, and 6.5 assists across 10 appearances. His passing ability remains a key asset even if his scoring has dipped.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement A Tough Road Ahead
 The Pacers enter Sunday's game looking for their third straight win after beating the New York Knicks in NBA Cup play on Friday. While dealing with their own injury concerns, Indiana has relied heavily on Pascal Siakam. The Sixers have managed to keep winning despite the heavy load on James and Joel Embiid. Tyrese Maxey led the team with 27 points in the win over Toronto, while Anfernee Simons added 17 off the bench. Rookie VJ Edgecombe also contributed 15 points, eight rebounds and eight assists in that game.
 Philadelphia has a difficult path in the NBA Cup after a heavy 24-point loss to the Cleveland Cavaliers on Nov. 6. That loss hurt their point differential significantly and put them behind in the group race. The team now needs big wins against tough opponents like the Heat and Pacers to stay in the hunt. Sixers Wire reports that the Sixers, Cavaliers, Heat, Knicks, and Pacers are among the teams battling for a next-round spot. The math for Philadelphia is unforgiving, and every point matters.
 Back-to-Back Concerns
 According to The Philadelphia Inquirer's Chris Hine, Thursday's absence was James' first that was not related to a back-to-back schedule. This makes his availability for Monday's game against the Brooklyn Nets a major question mark. The team must decide if playing Sunday is worth the risk of burning him out for the road trip. James has four full days of rest before Sunday, which gave him extra recovery time.
 LeBron James has not been officially confirmed as a starter yet, though his absence from the injury report suggests he is expected to play.
